#Graph 1: mean curves
summary_dat <- dat %>%
  group_by(condition, delay_ms) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(probability_rating))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  summary_dat,
  aes(
    x = delay_ms,
    y = mean_rating,
    color = condition,
    group = condition
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 50,
    linetype = "dashed",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_rating - se,
      ymax = mean_rating + se
    ),
    width = 15
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_color_discrete(
    labels = c(intact = "Agent", scrambled = "Object")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Temporal delay (ms)",
    y = "Mean causal judgment",
    color = "Condition"
  )

model_dat <- dat %>%
  select(participant, condition, delay_ms, probability_rating) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(participant),
    !is.na(condition),
    !is.na(delay_ms),
    !is.na(probability_rating)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

  group_by(participant, condition) %>%
  summarise(

library(mgcv)

gamm_test <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "REML" 
)

summary(gamm_test)
## 
## Family: gaussian 
## Link function: identity 
## 
## Formula:
## probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, k = 8) + s(participant, 
##     bs = "re")
## 
## Parametric coefficients:
##                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          68.225      4.164  16.386   <2e-16 ***
## conditionscrambled  -13.191      6.197  -2.129   0.0338 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Approximate significance of smooth terms:
##                   edf Ref.df      F p-value    
## s(delay_ms)     6.233  6.801 37.241  <2e-16 ***
## s(participant) 26.001 29.000  8.683  <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## R-sq.(adj) =  0.511   Deviance explained = 54.2%
## -REML =   2427  Scale est. = 517.18    n = 526
gamm <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 8) + #Give each condition its own nonlinear temporal curve.
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(gamm)
## 
## Family: gaussian 
## Link function: identity 
## 
## Formula:
## probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, by = condition, 
##     k = 8) + s(participant, bs = "re")
## 
## Parametric coefficients:
##                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          68.228      4.164  16.385   <2e-16 ***
## conditionscrambled  -13.190      6.197  -2.128   0.0338 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Approximate significance of smooth terms:
##                                   edf Ref.df      F p-value    
## s(delay_ms):conditionintact     5.038  5.924 17.745  <2e-16 ***
## s(delay_ms):conditionscrambled  6.184  6.776 22.519  <2e-16 ***
## s(participant)                 26.017 29.000  8.735  <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## R-sq.(adj) =  0.514   Deviance explained = 54.9%
## -REML = 2429.2  Scale est. = 514.5     n = 526
gam.check(gamm_test)

## 
## Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
## full convergence after 6 iterations.
## Gradient range [-1.446831e-05,7.899903e-06]
## (score 2427.048 & scale 517.1761).
## Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [2.052232,262.2009].
## Model rank =  40 / 40 
## 
## Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
## indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
## 
##                   k'   edf k-index p-value
## s(delay_ms)     7.00  6.23    1.03     0.7
## s(participant) 31.00 26.00      NA      NA
plot(gamm, pages = 1)

gam.check(gamm)

## 
## Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
## full convergence after 7 iterations.
## Gradient range [-1.2191e-06,3.224821e-07]
## (score 2429.151 & scale 514.503).
## Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [1.591841,261.7183].
## Model rank =  47 / 47 
## 
## Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
## indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
## 
##                                   k'   edf k-index p-value
## s(delay_ms):conditionintact     7.00  5.04    1.01    0.56
## s(delay_ms):conditionscrambled  7.00  6.18    1.01    0.61
## s(participant)                 31.00 26.02      NA      NA
model_diff <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML" 
)
model_same <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML"
)
#Graph 2, ANOVA Results Table

anova(model_same, model_diff, test = "Chisq") #whether the two-curve model fits significantly better than the shared-curve model. Answer: Yes, the two temporal curves differ in pilot data.
## Analysis of Deviance Table
## 
## Model 1: probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, k = 8) + s(participant, 
##     bs = "re")
## Model 2: probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, by = condition, 
##     k = 8) + s(participant, bs = "re")
##   Resid. Df Resid. Dev     Df Deviance Pr(>Chi)
## 1    487.96     254587                         
## 2    481.55     250823 6.4022   3763.6   0.3344
# Create prediction data
newdat <- expand.grid(
  delay_ms = seq(
    min(model_dat$delay_ms),
    max(model_dat$delay_ms),
    length.out = 300
  ),
  condition = levels(model_dat$condition),
  participant = NA
)

# Make sure participant has the same factor structure as in the model
newdat$participant <- factor(
  newdat$participant,
  levels = levels(model_dat$participant)
)

# Predict causal judgment
pred <- predict(
  model_diff,
  newdata = newdat,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

# Add predicted values
newdat$fit <- pred$fit
newdat$se <- pred$se.fit

# 95% confidence interval
newdat$lower <- newdat$fit - 1.96 * newdat$se
newdat$upper <- newdat$fit + 1.96 * newdat$se
head(newdat)

## 6  -966.5552    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
#predicted results visualization
#1.Create prediction data using an actual participant
levels(model_dat$participant)
##  [1] "s003" "s005" "s006" "s007" "s008" "s009" "s010" "s011" "s012" "s013"
## [11] "s014" "s015" "s018" "s020" "s021" "s022" "s023" "s024" "s025" "s026"
## [21] "s027" "s028" "s029" "s030" "s031" "s032" "s034" "s036" "s037" "s038"

newdat <- expand.grid(
  delay_ms = seq(
    min(model_dat$delay_ms),
    max(model_dat$delay_ms),
    length.out = 300
  ),
  condition = levels(model_dat$condition),
  participant = levels(model_dat$participant)[1]
)

pred <- predict(
  gamm,
  newdata = newdat,
  se.fit = TRUE,
  exclude = "s(participant)"
)
#2.Add the confidence intervals
newdat$fit <- as.numeric(pred$fit)
newdat$se <- as.numeric(pred$se.fit)

newdat$lower <- newdat$fit - 1.96 * newdat$se
newdat$upper <- newdat$fit + 1.96 * newdat$se

summary(newdat$fit)
